title: The coin
summary: A coin from the crowd hits you above the eye taking a corner. The police find the man who threw it, and he writes to you. A season on, there's a man in the family stand with his daughter.

ends.title: The letter back
ends.text: A man threw a coin at you and wrote to say sorry. You wrote back. He sits in the family stand now with his daughter.

ends.title: The ban
ends.text: A man threw a coin and got a three-year ban. You didn't read his letter.

event.title: A pound coin
event.speaker: manager
setup: Taking a corner in front of the away end, something hits you above the eye. A pound coin. Three stitches at half time.

On Tuesday {manager.name} hands you a letter the police have passed on. Very neat handwriting. "I threw the coin. I've got a daughter of eight and she saw. I'm not asking for anything. I wanted to say sorry to your face, and I can't."

say: "Up to you what you do with it. The club's lawyer wants it for court."

replies.label: Give it to the club's lawyer.
Don't read the rest. Bin it.

wrote.text: You write four lines. You say the stitches are fine, and that his daughter should come to a game with him, in the family stand. You don't know why you say that.

lawyer.text: The lawyer reads it out in court as proof he knew what he'd done. He gets a three-year ban.

binned.text: It goes in the bin in the boot room. He gets a three-year ban. You never read the rest.

beats.title: The family stand

event.title: The family stand
event.speaker: manager
setup: A season on. Warming up, you spot a man in the family stand with a girl of nine. He's not looking at you. She is, and she's holding up a pound coin.

outcomes.text: She gives you the coin. "Dad says it's yours." He shakes your hand and can't say anything. You keep the coin.
It isn't him. It's just a girl who found a pound. You sign her programme anyway.
You wave once. She waves back with the coin. He keeps his eyes on the pitch.
You don't know if it's him. You'll never know.
